display_title: Jay-Z to Headline Super Bowl Halftime
display_title_he: ג'יי-זי יופיע במופע המחצית של הסופרבול
short_summary: Rapper and entertainment mogul Jay-Z will headline the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show at SoFi Stadium in California. The announcement marks the first time the Roc Nation founder will perform on the stage he has helped curate since 2019.

paragraphs: After spending years orchestrating one of the world's most scrutinized entertainment spectacles from behind the scenes, rap mogul Jay-Z will finally step into the spotlight himself. The National Football League, Apple Music, and his entertainment enterprise Roc Nation announced that the veteran artist will headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show on February 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

The booking represents a notable full-circle milestone for the 56-year-old performer, whose legal name is Shawn Carter. Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to oversee and advise on the league's musical presentations, beginning with the co-headlined performance by Shakira and Jennifer Lopez in 2020. Over the past seven years, Carter played an instrumental role in curating halftime lineups that featured artists such as The Weeknd, Rihanna, Usher, and Kendrick Lamar, whose 2025 performance set historical viewership records. Yet, despite his pivotal behind-the-scenes influence, Carter had resisted taking the stage himself until now.

According to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, the league had long harbored hopes that Carter would eventually perform. Goodell recalled that during initial contract negotiations in 2019, his primary request was for the rapper to perform whenever the timing felt appropriate. Carter, reflecting on his artistic trajectory, described the progression from his 1996 debut album Reasonable Doubt to the Super Bowl stage as a sustained realization of his ambitions across three decades of music and cultural influence.

The announcement coincides with Carter celebrating the 30th anniversary of Reasonable Doubt, an occasion he marked with recent stadium concerts in New York and London, as well as two performances at SoFi Stadium. Over his career, Carter has accumulated 25 Grammy Awards across 89 nominations, gained induction into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2017, and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021. However, some music commentators had questioned whether he would ever headline the game, given that his last solo studio album, 4:44, was released in 2017, followed by a collaborative project with his wife, Beyoncé, in 2018.

Beyond musical considerations, Carter's upcoming performance arrives amid persistent cultural dialogue surrounding his business relationship with the football league. When Roc Nation signed its partnership, critics questioned whether aligning with the NFL compromised social justice advocacy, particularly in light of the league's contentious handling of former quarterback Colin Kaepernick's racial injustice protests. Cultural observers have noted that Carter has consistently navigated the intersection of corporate capitalism and Black advocacy, a duality recently examined in his documentary project Jay-Z in 8 alongside producer Rick Rubin.

Anticipation is now turning toward which guest artists might accompany Carter during the televised performance, with widespread public curiosity centering on potential appearances by previous collaborators, including Beyoncé. Regardless of who joins him, Carter will transition from power broker to central performer on American television's most visible musical platform.
